claims.claim: The PSR's final report (6 March 2025) found Mastercard and Visa raised core scheme and processing fees to UK acquirers by at least 25% since 2017, costing businesses at least £170m a year.
claims.quote: increased their core scheme and processing fees to acquirers by at least 25% since 2017, costing businesses at least £170million extra per year
claims.title: MR22/1.10 Market review of card scheme and processing fees: final report
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: The PSR final report also found poor fee information imposed costs on acquirers and merchants, including small retailers.
claims.quote: a lack of easy-to-understand fee information has led to costs for acquirers and merchants, including small retailers.
claims.title: MR22/1.10 Market review of card scheme and processing fees: final report
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: The PSR's headline finding is that Mastercard and Visa do not face competition in scheme and processing services, with fees rising and unclear pricing for businesses.
claims.quote: Mastercard and Visa don’t face competition with fees rising and a lack of clarity on how much businesses will have to pay
claims.title: Market review into card scheme and processing fees
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: On 30 July 2026 the PSR gave two final specific directions (SD22, SD23) to Mastercard and Visa implementing the ITC remedy and the Pricing Governance remedy.
claims.quote: We are giving two final specific directions to Mastercard and Visa (the schemes) to implement the Information, transparency and complexity (ITC) remedy
claims.title: PS26/1: Market review of card scheme and processing fees: Final decision
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: The ITC Direction requires the schemes to give acquirers clearer, more detailed fee information including data to reconcile fees with the transactions that generated them.
claims.quote: provide acquirers with clearer and more detailed information about the scheme and processing fees they are charged, including information to help reconcile fees
claims.title: PS26/1: Market review of card scheme and processing fees: Final decision
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: Pricing Governance Direction applies to relevant fee decisions from end November 2026; substantive ITC requirements apply from end July 2027.
claims.quote: Relevant fee decisions must comply with the Pricing Governance Direction from end of November 2026
claims.title: PS26/1: Market review of card scheme and processing fees: Final decision
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Same page: 'the substantive requirements of the ITC Direction apply from end of July 2027'. PSR revised materiality thresholds after consultation; SD22 page lists an Aug 2026 decision on requests to extend the ITC Standard B implementation period.

claims.claim: Specific Direction 22 scopes the ITC remedy to scheme and processing fees on card transactions initiated from a UK point of sale, covering existing, new and modified fees.
claims.quote: modified scheme and processing fees applicable to card transactions initiated from a UK point of sale
claims.title: Specific direction 22
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: A third PSR remedy, regulatory financial reporting, went to consultation on 21 May 2026 (CP26/1), requiring a UK card-operations P&L from Mastercard and Visa because margins looked higher than expected under competition.
claims.quote: the PSR found evidence consistent with a finding that the schemes’ profit margins are higher than expected in competitive markets.
claims.title: PSR to consult on UK profitability reporting for Mastercard and Visa
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: PSR MD David Geale said scheme fee increases had not been shown to reflect underlying costs.
claims.quote: Scheme fees have risen substantially in recent years, and we have not seen clear evidence that these increases reflect underlying costs.
claims.title: PSR to consult on UK profitability reporting for Mastercard and Visa
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: The RBA review ran in three phases: Issues Paper (Oct 2024), Consultation Paper (Jul 2025), Conclusions Paper (Mar 2026), with an issuer cost study in Aug 2025 and FAQs in Jul 2026.
claims.quote: Phase 3 – release of a Conclusions Paper to set out the PSB’s final decisions and package of policy reforms.
claims.title: About Review of Retail Payments Regulation
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: The RBA decided surcharging on eftpos, Mastercard and Visa debit and credit cards should end from 1 October 2026, by lifting the prohibition on scheme no-surcharge rules.
claims.quote: The RBA will lift the prohibition on ‘no-surcharge’ rules for all currently designated card networks (eftpos, Mastercard and Visa).
claims.title: Executive Summary – Review of Merchant Card Payment Costs and Surcharging – Conclusions Paper
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Amex (three-party) is not designated; merchants' ability to surcharge Amex deferred to a mid-2026 review under the amended PSRA.

claims.claim: The RBA expects the new and reduced interchange caps to lower merchants' wholesale card costs by around A$910 million a year, mainly benefiting small merchants.
claims.quote: lowering wholesale card payment costs for merchants by around $910 million per year through reducing interchange caps on domestic-issued cards
claims.title: Executive Summary – Review of Merchant Card Payment Costs and Surcharging – Conclusions Paper
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: RBA final interchange settings: debit cap lowered to 8 cents (or 0.16%), consumer credit cap to 0.3% with benchmark abolished, commercial credit kept at 0.8%, and new caps on foreign-issued cards.
claims.quote: lower the cap on domestic-issued consumer credit card interchange to 0.3 per cent and abolish the benchmark
claims.title: 3. Interchange Fees – Conclusions Paper
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Separate commercial cap kept explicitly to preserve competitive tension with American Express, the largest commercial issuer. Foreign-card cap effective 1 April 2027; domestic changes 1 October 2026. Page updated 19 June 2026 with a factual correction.

claims.claim: RBA data: acquirers paid A$992m net scheme fees on domestic transactions in 2024/25 (10.5bp, 17.8% of MSF), plus A$514m on cross-border acquiring at 158bp.
claims.quote: Scheme fees paid by acquirers tend to account for around one-sixth of Australian merchants’ domestic-issued card transaction costs
claims.title: 4. Scheme Fees – Conclusions Paper
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Table 9 covers fees paid to eftpos, Mastercard and Visa combined.

claims.claim: The RBA concluded scheme fees, especially on credit, are not effectively competitively constrained; LCR plus eftpos has disciplined debit scheme fees while credit has no equivalent mechanism.
claims.quote: there is no equivalent mechanism to encourage competition between the international card networks for credit card transactions.
claims.title: 4. Scheme Fees – Conclusions Paper
claims.label: Verified

claims.claim: Instead of a scheme fee cap, the RBA set an expectation that networks publish 'Scheme Fee Roadmaps' by 1 April 2027 covering six-month notice, fee classification, machine-readable invoices and error remediation.
claims.quote: The PSB expects card networks to publish these Roadmaps and make them available to the RBA for publication on its website by 1 April 2027.
claims.title: 4. Scheme Fees – Conclusions Paper
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Box D principles: 6-month minimum notice for fee changes and no re-change for a further 6 months; mandatory/optional/behavioural classification; machine-readable invoices at no cost; remediation for all affected participants; clear opt-out for optional fees.

claims.claim: Participants told the RBA scheme fee complexity is deliberate and that strict confidentiality terms stop them comparing pricing or even understanding their own bills; the RBA kept price caps and credit LCR as escalation options.
claims.quote: Most submissions received by the RBA noted exceptionally strict confidentiality terms and information restrictions in their contractual arrangements with the card networks
claims.title: 4. Scheme Fees – Conclusions Paper
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Escalation options named: a standard on scheme fee practices, scheme fee price caps, dual-network credit cards and LCR for credit.

claims.claim: The RBA kept the 'expectations' approach to in-person least-cost routing rather than a mandate; 84% of merchants had LCR enabled by December 2025, and large issuers must keep issuing dual-network debit cards.
claims.quote: The share of merchants with LCR enabled for in-person transactions had risen from 50 per cent in June 2022 to 84 per cent
claims.title: 7. Least-cost Routing of Debit Card Transactions – Conclusions Paper
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Issuers above 1% of debit value expected to provision both networks in all form factors; LCR for online/mobile wallets deferred to a mid-2026 consultation.

claims.claim: LCR has driven dual-network debit interchange to around 6 cents, below the 8-cent benchmark; one network argued the status quo entrenches eftpos as the default on the back of debit cards.
claims.quote: A network stated that the status quo entrenches eftpos as the default network on the back of debit cards.
claims.title: 7. Least-cost Routing of Debit Card Transactions – Conclusions Paper
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Stakeholder view reported in the RBA paper; network not named.

claims.claim: The RBA will require eftpos, Mastercard, Visa and large acquirers to publish the fees they charge, and acquirers to publish merchant service fees and a measure of interchange pass-through.
claims.quote: eftpos, Mastercard, Visa and large acquirers will have to publish the fees they charge, which will help businesses check how their fees compare.
claims.title: In Brief: Merchant Card Payment Costs and Surcharging – March 2026
claims.label: Verified
claims.note: Some transparency measures take effect 1 April 2027.
